property_summary: For any call with a non-zero msg.value, the reference contract requires exactly 10 ether and reverts otherwise, while the buggy version allows any call with 0 ether to proceed without revert.

When a non-zero msg.value is sent with block.timestamp ≤ pastBlockTime, the reference C always reverts (because the first require(msg.value == 10 ether) passes, then the second require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) fails), but the buggy C never reaches the second require and silently accepts the call.

For any call to the fallback, the reference C always reverts unless msg.value is exactly 10 ether; the buggy C allows a call with 0 ether to succeed when block.timestamp > pastBlockTime, violating the invariant that successful fallback calls must have msg.value == 10 ether.

For any call to the fallback, if the call succeeds then either msg.value == 10 ether or pastBlockTime is unchanged; the buggy version allows a 0 ether call to succeed and update pastBlockTime, breaking this invariant.

After any sequence of fallback calls, if block.timestamp is strictly greater than the previous fallback's timestamp, pastBlockTime must equal block.timestamp of the last successful call; the mutant breaks this by allowing calls with msg.value != 10 ether to update pastBlockTime without sending value.
For any call to fallback() that does not revert, the contract's balance must increase by exactly 10 ether; the mutant allows a call with 0 ether to succeed without increasing balance.
After a successful call to fallback, the contract's balance is exactly 10 ether; the mutant violates this by allowing calls with 0 ether to succeed, resulting in a balance of 0 ether.
After a successful call to fallback, the contract balance must be at least 10 ether; the mutant allows a call with msg.value != 10 ether to succeed, resulting in a balance less than 10 ether.
After a successful fallback call with msg.value != 10 ether, pastBlockTime must not increase; the mutant increases it without the required ether.

The reference contract ensures pastBlockTime strictly increases with each successful call, preventing any two calls from executing at the same timestamp; the buggy version allows same-block calls, causing a second call to update pastBlockTime without a transfer when block.number % 15 != 0.

For any sequence of fallback calls, the reference contract ensures that pastBlockTime never equals the previous call's pastBlockTime after a non-transfer call, while the buggy version allows a second same-block call where pastBlockTime remains unchanged and no transfer occurs.

In the reference, every successful fallback call strictly increases pastBlockTime, so two calls at the same block.timestamp are impossible. In the mutant, two calls at the same block.timestamp can both succeed, causing a second call to update pastBlockTime without a transfer when block.number % 15 == 0, leaving the contract balance unchanged after the second call.
Multiple calls to fallback within the same block can only succeed once in the reference contract, but the mutant allows multiple successful calls in the same block.

After any sequence of fallback calls, the value of pastBlockTime should always equal the block.timestamp of the most recent successful call; the mutant sets it to 1, so a subsequent call can fail the timestamp require when block.timestamp ≤ 1.

For any two successful calls to the fallback function, the pastBlockTime after the second call must be greater than the pastBlockTime after the first call; the mutant sets pastBlockTime to 1, violating this monotonic increase.

After any successful call to fallback, pastBlockTime must equal the block.timestamp of that call; the mutant sets it to 1 instead, so subsequent calls with block.timestamp > 1 can succeed but the value will be wrong.

For any two successful fallback calls where the second call is made with a block.timestamp after the first call's block.timestamp, the pastBlockTime must always be greater than or equal to the timestamp of the first call; the mutant sets pastBlockTime to 1, so when the second call is made at a timestamp greater than 1, pastBlockTime will be less than the first call's timestamp.
After a successful fallback call, the pastBlockTime must always equal block.timestamp; the bug fails to update it, allowing a subsequent call in the same block to bypass the timestamp check.

After two successful fallback calls in the same block, pastBlockTime must be updated after each call, so the second call must revert; the bug fails to update pastBlockTime, allowing the second call to succeed.

For any sequence of successful fallback calls, if a call transfers the full balance, a subsequent call in the same block (with the required 10 ether sent again) must revert; the bug fails to update pastBlockTime, allowing the subsequent call to succeed after a transfer empties the contract.

After any successful fallback execution that does not trigger a transfer, the contract balance must equal the total Ether sent via all successful fallback calls (i.e., no Ether is erroneously retained); the bug fails to update pastBlockTime, which can allow a subsequent successful call in the same block that triggers a transfer, causing the contract to hold less Ether than expected.

For the correct contract, after any admissible fallback call the contract balance is either nonzero (if block.number is divisible by 15) or zero (if not); the buggy version incorrectly transfers the balance on non-multiples instead.

For any admissible fallback call, the contract's balance is either 0 if block.number is not a multiple of 15, or 10 ether if it is; the mutant transfers the balance on non-multiples and keeps 0 on multiples, violating this relationship.

After a successful fallback call, if block.number is a multiple of 15 the contract balance must be 0; the mutant drains on non‑multiples so for some input where block.number%15==0 the balance remains 10 ether, violating the invariant.
